case_number: Civil Appeal No. of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (Civil) Nos. of 2012, 36222 of 2018, 36221 of 2018, 29577 of 2018, 17007 of 2017)

parties.respondent: Smt. Shashi Kiran & Ors., C.L. Khanna (Retd.) & Ors., Dr. S.N. Singh, Dr. Santosh Kaur Sangari & Ors., N.C. Bakshi & Ors.

summary: The appeals were filed by the University of Delhi challenging the Delhi High Court's judgment upholding the rights of teaching staff to opt for the General Provident Fund (GPF) and pension scheme instead of the Contributory Provident Fund (CPF). The dispute arose from the application of a 1987 Central Government policy change deeming CPF beneficiaries in service on 1.1.1986 to have automatically transferred to GPF unless they opted out by 30.9.1987. The University adopted similar rules under Statute 28-A. Though 2611 employees opted to remain under CPF, the University issued extensions for opting out. The High Court upheld the employees' right to exercise the option beyond the original deadline. The Supreme Court examined the validity of these extensions and the binding effect of the University's adoption of Central Government pension reforms. The core issue was whether the University could lawfully grant extensions and whether employees retained a right to opt out after the stipulated date.
legal_provisions_cited: Statute 28-A of the University of Delhi
Department of Personnel and Training O.M. No. F 3 (1) - Pension Unit/85 dated 06.06.1985
final_judgment: The appeals were disposed of with directions to the University to process the pending opt-out applications in accordance with law and the principles of fairness, equity, and consistency with the original scheme framework.
